expected_level_description: You can: - manage configuration management for the organisation, ensuring value for the business and adherence to company policies - ensure that changes to assets are recorded and controlled appropriately - advocate organisational commitment to asset control

You can: - lead investigative work into problems and opportunities in existing processes - lead the collection of information and creation of recommendations for improvements - absorb large amounts of conflicting information and use it to produce solutions

You can: - analyse current processes, and identify and implement opportunities to optimise them - lead and develop a team of experts to deliver service improvements - help to evaluate and establish requirements for the implementation of changes by setting policy and standards
You can: - use data analytics skills to make decisions that enhance business performance
You can: - take accountability for issues that occur and be proactive in searching for potential problems - achieve excellent user outcomes
You can: - show you have an expert certificate in the service management framework qualification - demonstrate an industry understanding of how to implement the framework into numerous environments

You can: - manage long-term strategic relationships with stakeholders, identifying where new connections need to be made and existing ones nurtured - direct the strategic approach for stakeholder relationships, establishing stakeholder objectives and ensuring these are clearly represented - act as a point of escalation if stakeholder relationships break down or become challenging for more junior members of the team - influence important senior stakeholders and arbitrate when blockers are escalated - facilitate discussions across high risk and complex areas or projects under constrained timelines
You can: - lead the design and implementation of strategy, directing the evaluation of strategies and policies to ensure business requirements are being met
You can: - show a thorough understanding of the technical concepts required for the role, and can explain how these fit into the wider technical landscape

You can: - give direction on which tools or methods to use - demonstrate experience in meeting the needs of users across a variety of channels - bring insight and expertise in how user needs have changed over time to ensure they're met by the business - apply strategic thinking to provide the best service for the end user

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload

You can: - lead data protection impact assessments and information sharing agreements - advise teams on lawful basis, consent, confidentiality, and retention - investigate incidents and recommend improvements
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - run the risk process for a directorate or programme - assess risks against the risk appetite and escalate them - report on risks to committees
You can: - line manage a team, setting objectives and running appraisals - support wellbeing and manage attendance, performance, and conduct - plan the team's development and succession
You can: - hold and manage a budget, forecasting and explaining variances - build a business case with costs and benefits
